(29 November 2017) | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2016–17 Saudi First Division|2016–17]] | nextseason = [[2018–19 Prince Mohammad bin Salman League|2018–19]] | updated = 4 May 2018 }} The '''2017–18 Prince Mohammad bin Salman League''' was the first season of the [[Prince Mohammad bin Salman League]] under its current name, and 41st season of the Saudi First Division since its establishment in 1976. The season started on 12 September 2017 and concluded on 18 April 2018.{{Cite news|title=صدورجدول الدور الأول لدوري الدرجة الأولى 2017-2018|url=http://thesaff.com.sa/NewsDetails.aspx?NewsID=16093|date=18 July 2017|accessdate=11 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170917032255/http://thesaff.com.sa/NewsDetails.aspx?NewsID=16093|archive-date=17 September 2017|url-status=dead}}{{Cite news |title=#لجنة_المسابقات تعلن جدول مواعيد مباريات الدور الثاني من دوري الأمير فيصل بن فهد لأندية الدرجة الأولى للمحترفين|url=https://twitter.com/saudiFF/status/930011448797028352|date=13 November 2017|accessdate=1 January 2018}} ==Overview== ===First Division rebranding=== On 19 September 2017, the General Sports Authority announced a rebrand; beginning with the 2017–18 season, the competition was known as the Prince [[Faisal bin Fahd]] League. As part of the rebranding, a new logo was introduced.{{cite web |website=Twitter.com |url=https://twitter.com/gsaksa/status/910174990351454208 |title=إطلاق اسم الأمير فيصل بن فهد على منافسات دوري الدرجة الأولى |publisher=gsa |date=19 September 2017 |accessdate=19 September 2017 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191215055523/https://twitter.com/gsaksa/status/910174990351454208 |archive-date=15 December 2019 }} On 9 February 2018, the General Sports Authority once again announced a rebrand; starting from the current season, the competition will be known as the Prince [[Mohammad bin Salman]] League.{{cite web |website= Twitter.com |url=https://twitter.com/Turki_alalshikh/status/961929088201056256|title= إطلاق اسم سيدي ولي العهد على دوري الدرجة الأولى ليصبح|publisher=gsa |date=9 February 2018}} ===Rule changes=== On 11 September 2017, the SAFF announced that the numbers of foreign players were increased from 2 players to 3 players. They also announced that the allowed number of substitutions per match was increased from 3 to 5.{{cite web |url= https://twitter.com/saudiFF/status/907172449267195905 |title=عددٌ من التغييرات طرأت على #دوري_الدرجة_الأولى_للمحترفين، تعرّف على أبرز تلك التغييرات قبل انطلاق الدوري غدً |publisher= SAFF |date=11 September 2017 |accessdate= 11 September 2017}} ==Teams== A total of 16 teams are contesting the league, including 11 sides from the [[2016–17 Saudi First Division|2016–17 season]], two relegated from the [[2016–17 Saudi Professional League|2016–17 Professional League]], and three promoted from the [[2016–17 Saudi Second Division|2016–17 Second Division]]. [[Al Kawkb Club|Al-Kawkab]] and [[Jeddah Club|Jeddah]] became the first two clubs to be promoted to the First Division, with both clubs finishing as group winners. [[Al-Mujazzel Club|Al-Mujazzel]] became the third and final club to be promoted, following a 5–1 win over [[Al-Ansar F.C.|Al-Ansar]] on 3 March 2017, to secure their return to the First Division after only a season's absence. Al-Kawkab returned to the First Division for the first time since the [[2013–14 Saudi First Division|2013–14 season]], and Jeddah will play in their first-ever season in the First Division since being re-branded. On 20 April 2017, [[Al-Wehda Club (Mecca)|Al-Wehda]] became the first side to be relegated from the [[2016–17 Saudi Professional League|Pro League]] following a 2–1 home defeat to [[Al-Fateh SC|Al-Fateh]].{{Cite news |title=رسمياً.. الوحدة يودع دوري جميل |url=http://www.dawryjameel.com/news/aljl/details/al-wehda-first-club-leave-jameel-league/ |publisher=dawryjameel |date=21 April 2017 |accessdate=21 May 2017 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170822175936/http://www.dawryjameel.com/news/aljl/details/al-wehda-first-club-leave-jameel-league/ |archivedate=22 August 2017 |url-status=dead }} This will be Al-Wehda's first season back to the First Division since the [[2014–15 Saudi First Division|2014–15 season]]. On 4 May 2017, [[Khaleej FC|Al-Khaleej]] were the 2nd side to be relegated from the Pro League after a 2–2 draw with [[Al-Faisaly FC|Al-Faisaly]], finishing 13th in the league.{{Cite news |title=الترتيب النهائي لفرق دوري جميل للمحترفين |url=http://www.dawryjameel.com/news/aljl/details/dawryjameel-teams/ |publisher=dawryjameel |date=4 May 2017 |accessdate=21 May 2017 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170822175415/http://www.dawryjameel.com/news/aljl/details/dawryjameel-teams/ |archivedate=22 August 2017 |url-status=dead }} This will also be Al-Khaleej's first season return to the First Division since the [[2013–14 Saudi First Division|2013–14 season]]. On 27 April 2017 [[Wej SC|Wej]] became the first club to be relegated to the Second Division following 2–1 loss to [[Hajer Club|Hajer]]. On the final matchday, both [[Al-Adalh FC|Al-Adalh]] and [[Al Jeel Club|Al-Jeel]] were relegated to the Second Division, with both clubs drawing their matches. ==Team changes== The following teams have changed division since the 2016–17 season. {{col-begin}} {{col-2}} === To Prince Mohammad bin Salman League === '''Promoted from [[2016–17 Saudi Second Division|Second Division]]''' * [[Al Kawkb Club|Al-Kawkab]] * [[Jeddah Club|Jeddah]] * [[Al-Mujazzel Club|Al-Mujazzel]] '''Relegated from [[2016–17 Saudi Professional League|Professional League]]''' * [[Khaleej FC|Al-Khaleej]] * [[Al-Wehda Club (Mecca)|Al-Wehda]] === From Prince Mohammad bin Salman League === '''Relegated to [[2017–18 Saudi Second Division|Second Division]]''' * [[Al-Adalh FC|Al-Adalh]] * [[Al Jeel Club|Al-Jeel]] * [[Wej SC|Wej]] '''Promoted to [[2017–18 Saudi Professional League|Professional League]]''' * [[Al-Feiha FC|Al-Feiha]] * [[Ohod Club|Ohod]] {{col-end}} ==Stadia and locations==
